B. Is this measure already running in Lapland wellbeing services county (or in the OYS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Travel and accommodation support for patients far from the university hospital. Patients who must travel for surgery or weeks of radiotherapy get a booked patient hotel, organised transport and a named contact, so that distance is not the reason to choose a non-curative treatment.
supported_en: Br J Cancer 2009 (northern England): patients with the longest travel time had odds of lung cancer surgery 0.60 times those of the nearest group.
not_supported_en: No study read shows that travel or lodging support raises the curative share, or by how much; the assumed 1 percentage point is not tested.
in_use_quote: Jos tulet pitkän matkan takaa eikä vointisi ole sellainen, että sinun tarvitsisi jäädä sairaalan vuodeosastolle, sinä ja läheisesi voitte majoittua sairaalan lähellä sijaitsevassa potilaskodissa.
missing_en: No page shows organised transport, booking done by staff or a named contact for patients who must travel.
summary_en: OYS runs a patient home with 63 beds 400–700 m from the hospital for patients who come from far away. The adult price is 41.98 euros a night, Kela pays part of it back, and patients book it themselves. Lapin keskussairaala also has a 5-bed patient hotel that patients book themselves. For the effect, the only study read is from northern England (Crawford et al., 2009). It links the longest travel time to lower odds of lung cancer surgery (OR 0.60), but it does not test any travel-support measure.
unanswered_en: I found no page on organised transport or a named travel contact for Lapland lung cancer patients treated at OYS, and no study measuring the effect of travel support.
